objective: One bounded attempt to prove the odd-loop identity, starting from the seam bijection that is exact on tori of height 3. Deliver a proof, a partial proof with its exact scope, or the obstruction met, with exhaustive and sampled checks.
status: Proved by ODD-LOOP-20261023-001B-P001 (V1 prose proof; every line configuration of 3 x 3 at shears 0 and 1, and 10,558 orientations from walks inside nine line events on tori up to 9 x 4 and 7 x 7, all passing; three controls rejected). The odd-loop identity holds on every square-lattice torus, at every shear and for every primitive class c: the two twists odd on c give the same probability that the strong components wind along c and nothing else. The proof is an explicit involution. It slides the second twist's seam onto the wall that bounds the lift of the canonical swap-invariant strong component from above in the cover along c, flips the bits of the wall edges whose end off the component is their head, and gauges back. No directed cycle changes, so every cycle statistic has the same law on the two events. Corollary: odd10 + odd01 - odd11 = twice the probability of an odd loop in a class = (1, 1) mod 2, so the consistency relation is equivalent to D equal to that quantity. The first attempt with straight inert bands is preserved: it is an involution only on bands avoiding the row above the default seam, and a stored 4 x 4 orientation breaks the unrestricted rule.
title: Proof attempt: the odd-loop identity
